questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: The engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection of the engine, check the engine oil level, coolant level, and the condition of hoses.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm other people.
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe.
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm other people.
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is selfish or pushy driving behavior.

questions.question: After a pre-trip inspection, what should you make sure to do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Close the service line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open both the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all trailer brakes. You will hear escaping air. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, together on any part of the vehicle.
Yes, together on the front of the vehicle.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires. All tires on a vehicle should be the same type and size.

questions.question: When does liquid surge occur?

options.text: In tanks that have not been used for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: In partially full tanks.
questions.explanation: Liquid surge happens when liquid moves around inside a partially full tank.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a skid?

options.text: It will make the skid worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will make the skid worse.
questions.explanation: If your trailer is skidding or jackknifing, release the brakes to help tires regain grip. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will only make the skid continue.

questions.question: What should you know about hearing trains at railroad crossings?

options.text: You will always hear an approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The operator may not sound the horn, or it may be prohibited in that area. Also, noise inside your vehicle may prevent you from hearing the train until it is very close.

questions.question: What does having anti-lock brakes on only one axle do?

options.text: It will give you better control while braking.
It will cause air brake problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will give you better control while braking.
questions.explanation: Even with anti-lock brakes on just one axle, you will have more braking control than without any anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: The trucks are often shiny and hard to see.
Drivers are often in a hurry and may not look before leaving the truck.
Packages often fall out onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers are often in a hurry and may not look before leaving the truck.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may be in a hurry and suddenly pull into traffic without warning, or step out of the vehicle without checking for traffic.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually occur?

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. With enough water, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph. It is more likely with under-inflated or worn tires.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: How should you take a highway curve?

options.text: At or slightly above the posted speed limit
Well below the posted speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have a high center of gravity and are likely to tip over on turns and curves. Take curves and ramps at speeds that are well below the posted limits.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating required on a placarded vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 B:C
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with an Underwriters Laboratories (UL) rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: How does fatigue affect a driver?

options.text: Makes them more careful than most drivers
Slows their ability to make critical decisions

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows their ability to make critical decisions
questions.explanation: Fatigued drivers are slower to spot or react to hazards. Drowsy drivers have trouble making critical decisions.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, how should you identify the hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: By using the shipping papers
questions.explanation: If you find a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials, as this could cause injury or death.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch the road ahead?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard
It is only important in heavy traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, what should the floor liner be made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Non-ferrous materials
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a tight floor liner made of non-metallic or non-ferrous material. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Push down gradually
questions.explanation: When stopping, push the brake pedal down gradually. Gradual braking helps you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over a trailer
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can overturn trailers. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip. Drivers should understand this effect and drive carefully.

questions.question: How can you best tell that your trailer has started to skid?

options.text: By checking the trailer in your mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: By checking the trailer in your mirrors
questions.explanation: The easiest way to notice that your trailer is jackknifing is to watch it in your mirrors. This also helps you spot skidding as early as possible.
